summary: Hourly postback lag causes provisional invoice to underreport prior-hour usage
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightGov sees their provisional invoice for 2026-02-24 underreport usage for the 18:00-19:00 UTC hour. Internal metering shows usage was posted late by ~12 minutes and the provisional invoice aggregation window omitted the late postback. This looks tied to the hourly postback aggregation job experiencing elevated lag (backpressure from the microbatch queue) during that window.

Impact:
- Customer-facing provisional invoice subtotal is ~32% lower for the affected hour, causing an alert on their finance side and potential downstream reconciliation failures.
- No permanent overcharge reported yet, but risk of surprise adjustments on final invoice when late postbacks are applied.

Environment:
- Production metering pipeline in us-east-1, hourly aggregation service (meter-agg-v2), provisional invoice generator (proinv-service).
impact: Customer provisional invoice underreports one hourly bucket; finance team escalated and paused automated charge reconciliations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate sustained microbatch backlog by sending parallel batch-embed jobs from a dedicated customer token for 90s.
2) Force a delayed postback by introducing 10s processing delay in the embed worker.
3) Trigger hourly aggregation window at :00 UTC.
4) Observe provisional invoice subtotal and compare to raw postback records.

(Engineering note: reproducer included to validate aggregation logic when postbacks arrive after window close but before invoice snapshot.)
logs:
meter-agg-v2 logs (2026-02-24T18:00:00Z - 19:15:00Z):
- 18:59:48Z INFO received postback (customer=brightgov, events=124)
- 19:00:00Z WARN window-close triggered, pending-postbacks=0
- 19:00:12Z ERROR late-postback detected, postback-arrival=00:12 after-window-close, decision=drop-from-provisional
- 19:00:30Z INFO reconciliation-job enqueued

Postback service traces: trace_id=trc_brightgov_0291 latencies peaked at 7200ms for commit to s3 cache.
Metric spikes: meter.postback.queue_latency p90=6.8s, meter.agg.window_skipped=1
investigation_notes: Confirmed provisional invoice snapshot excludes postbacks arriving > window_grace (config default 5s).
Observed transient queue buildup in microbatch workers from 18:58:30Z to 19:00:20Z related to a concurrent large batch-job from a different enterprise customer which consumed worker slots.
Config check: window_grace configured to 5s for proinv-service in prod; postback retries arrive up to 120s after initial attempt.

Hypothesis: Provisional snapshot timing + conservative grace window meant legitimate late postbacks were excluded. Long-term fix may need to be more tolerant for provisional calculations or replay into provisional aggregator.
Cross-ref: similar pattern in SUP-912345 where late stream commits affected daily smoothing.
comments: Support (Lena Torres): Thanks for filing, Marcus. We've validated the discrepancy and escalated to Billing Ops. I'll coordinate with Metering infra to capture the late postbacks and hold final invoice adjustments while we investigate.

Customer (Aaron Patel, BrightGov): We rely on provisional invoices for internal monthly estimates — can you confirm if this will affect our March budget report? We need a workaround if not fixed within 48 hours.

Billing Ops (Rhea Singh): We've pulled the raw postbacks and can retroactively include the late arrivals before final invoice generation. Recalculating provisional is possible but will require enforcement from finance to accept an amended provisional snapshot.

Metering Infra (Diego Martinez): Identified microbatch consumer saturation between 18:58-19:01. Patch proposed to increase postback-ack worker pool by +2 for hot hours. Also evaluating increasing proinv window_grace to 30s behind a feature flag.

Support (Lena Torres): Temporary workaround applied: set feature-flag proinv.grace=30s for us-east for the next 24 hours to capture late postbacks while we patch scaling behavior. Customers impacted have been notified.
workarounds: Applied feature-flag proinv.grace=30s in us-east for 24h to include late postbacks in provisional aggregation.
Billing Ops to generate an amended provisional invoice for BrightGov and flag the change with explanation to their finance contact.
If customers need deterministic hourly estimates, recommend using event-level usage reports (raw_postbacks_export) until permanent fix.
resolution_notes: Temporarily increased provisional grace window for us-east and scaled postback workers to reduce queue pressure. Billing Ops issued an amended provisional invoice to BrightGov and marked the change as non-billable for final invoice reconciliation to avoid double-billing. Monitoring configured to alert on meter.postback.queue_latency > 3s during hourly close.
root_cause: Hourly aggregation dropped legitimate postbacks that arrived just outside the configured grace window (5s) during a transient microbatch worker saturation event. The grace window was insufficient given observed postback delivery latencies under load.
follow_up_actions: Ship meter-agg-v2 patch to auto-extend window_grace when queue_latency > 2s (dev sprint 2026-03-05).
Increase default proinv.window_grace to 30s for enterprise customers while we monitor impact (ops runbook update).
Add canary test that simulates late postbacks in pre-prod to validate provisional snapshots before rollout.
Convene postmortem with SRE, Billing Ops, and Customer Success to review communication cadence for provisional invoice adjustments (owner: Rhea Singh, due 2026-03-04).
